Follow the brief exactly: its genre, audience, structure and target length (within 10% either way). Write the piece itself and nothing else — no preamble, no notes to the editor, no closing remarks, no questions. Use plain headings in the house style described; do not use markdown bold or emphasis inside paragraphs. Where the brief asks for charts or figures, refer to them by number and give their titles, notes and sources as text; do not draw them. Do not mention that you are an AI or that a brief exists.

BRIEF

Write Section 6, "General discussion", of about 1,400 words for an empirical article in PLOS ONE, with the subsections 6.1 Theoretical contributions, 6.2 Practical implications, and 6.3 Limitations and future research, preceded by a short opening discussion.

The study: a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 366 employees across China, analysed with PLS-SEM, framed by Uses and Gratifications Theory. It examines how two motivations for using generative AI tools at work — cognitive use (information and knowledge seeking) and social use (interaction and networking) — relate to employees' innovative job performance, through knowledge transfer behaviours and resource acquisition capabilities as mediators and job satisfaction as a further mediating mechanism.

Write in the register of the journal: interpret the pattern of results in terms of the theory, state the theoretical contributions, give concrete implications for managers and organisations deploying generative AI, acknowledge the design's limitations (cross-sectional data, self-report, single-country sample, the scope of the constructs) and propose future research, using numbered reference citations in square brackets as PLOS ONE does. Close with a one-paragraph conclusion.

CITATION RULE

Cite evidence where you can, using the citation style the brief specifies. Cite only sources you are confident exist and say what they found; where you are not confident of a source, make the claim without a citation or do not make it. Do not invent survey figures: where you do not have a figure, describe the evidence qualitatively. Target length: 1400 words.
